original_value: Grey‐level co‐occurrence matrix (GLCM) is a widely used texture feature descriptor that is extracted from grey‐level images. A considerable amount of work in the literature has been done trying to combine colour with GLCM features. The aim of this study is to examine the effect of integrating colour with GLCM. To this end, 14 descriptors that have been proposed in literature based on different colour combining approaches, four Convolutional Neural Networks‐based, two aggregation‐based, and five other handcrafted descriptors have been engaged in this comparison. Five widely known data sets have been used to experimentally evaluate each descriptor. The evaluation has been conducted for image classification and image retrieval. Results indicated that there is no co‐occurrence‐matrix‐based descriptor that overcomes all the others in all data sets. Nevertheless, some descriptors have shown a remarkably higher performance than the others.

result.paraphrase: Grey-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) is a widely used texture descriptor extracted from grey-level images. Much of the literature has focused on combining colour with GLCM features. This study investigates the effect of integrating colour into GLCM. To do so, 14 descriptors proposed in the literature based on different colour-combining approaches, four based on Convolutional Neural Networks, two aggregation-based descriptors, and five other handcrafted descriptors were included in the comparison. Five well-known datasets were used to experimentally assess each descriptor. The evaluation covered both image classification and image retrieval. The results showed that no co-occurrence-matrix-based descriptor outperformed all others across every dataset. Even so, some descriptors achieved markedly better performance than the rest.
